name: Vostok Industrial Hardshell Helm
description:
A reinforced composite helmet originally designed for Crucible heavy-industry workers operating in foundry and demolition environments. The outer shell is layered carbon-ceramic rated for impact, heat, and particulate deflection. An internal gel-cushion liner auto-adjusts to head geometry.

The Vostok has migrated from industrial sites to Shelf-district security teams and unlicensed pit-fighting circuits, where its durability and low cost make it the default head protection for people who can't afford military-grade gear.
functionality: Impact protection, heat resistance, particulate filtering
what_it_says: You work where things fall, explode, or get thrown at your head. You chose function over style because you're still alive.
story_hooks: A batch of Vostok helms shipped to a Shelf clinic were found to contain embedded micro-transmitters — someone was tracking every wearer's location.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, angular helmet with pronounced forward-jutting brow ridge and reinforced temple panels. Sits low on the head with a bulky, utilitarian silhouette. Suggests protection over aesthetics—something built to absorb punishment rather than turn heads.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight around the crown and temples, with internal gel-padding that molds to individual skull geometry. Chin strap runs snug but not restrictive. Peripheral vision slightly reduced by the aggressive brow angle.
physical_description.primary_material: Layered carbon-ceramic composite shell with embedded shock-absorption gel liner. Exterior has a semi-matte industrial finish; interior padding is soft and slightly tacky to the touch.
physical_description.texture: Outer shell is smooth but not glossy—finely textured from the molding process, with faint grid-pattern reinforcement lines visible under certain angles. The carbon weave creates subtle micro-ridges. Liner feels gel-like, yielding under pressure.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with charcoal and matte-black reinforcement panels. Minimal branding—small Crucible Genomics logo stamped in weathered silver on the left temple. Some units show faded safety-yellow accent stripes (original foundry requirement).
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap chin strap with friction-fit adjustment, rated for quick-release impact scenarios. Side-panel access vents sealed with micro-magnetic clips.
distinctive_features: Pronounced carbon-ceramic brow ridge designed to deflect downward strikes
Integrated ventilation grid along temples to prevent heat buildup
Auto-adjusting internal gel-liner conforms to head shape within 60 seconds of wear
Reinforced impact zones at temples and back-skull marked by raised ridges
Minimal optical cutout—maximizes protective coverage at cost of peripheral awareness
Burnished brass grommets for attachment points (modular visor/filter add-ons)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Affordable, durable, but visibly industrial. Signals working-class or sub-grade origins but also street credibility in Shelf districts and fighting communities.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Crucible foundry crews, demolition teams, unlicensed pit fighters, and Shelf-district security contractors. Associated with people in dangerous, low-paying work who prioritize protection over status. In pit-fighting circles, it's a mark of scrappy resilience. Among corpo types, it reads as either slumming or a deliberate anti-fashion statement.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually weathered—scuffed outer shell, faded safety markings, gel liner compressed on one side from habitual wear. Chin strap shows creasing from regular use. Rarely pristine; owners wear them hard.
